summary: Weekly sync for Voltix quantization pilot. Reviewed INT8 vs FP8 deltas, surfaced a small cluster of quality regressions on long-form summarization prompts, discussed config levers (dynamic kv/prefix cache, beam/temperature knobs, per-model fallback), and planned Dedicated benchmark for SLA readiness. Action items assigned for re-runs, prompt curation, and legal/SLA readout.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-17
Start: 10:30 AM PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Connor (CSM), Sam (Voltix ML), Jordan (Voltix Infra), Lina (Voltix Sec), Mei (Voltix Product)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everybody, thanks for joining, just a quick agenda — status on the INT8 pilot runs, look at the FP8 comparison that Priya ran yesterday, triage the regressed prompt set, and then talk about next steps for SLA / dedicated runs. Any additions?
[00:17] Sam: Nope, that's good. We wanna focus on the long-form summarization hits — some of the worst diffs are there.
[00:28] Priya: I posted the quick perf table in the pilot sheet, the INT8 baseline with default cache had about a 1.9x token throughput improvement and latency down ~25% at p50 but p99 is a little noisier, I pulled fp8 numbers too but I want to underline that the fp8 runs were on a different host kernel so not exactly apples to apples.
[00:52] Jordan: When you say noisy p99, are we seeing tail spikes because of batching, or is it GPU scheduling / context switch?
[01:03] Priya: Good question — initial trace suggests a mix: small kernel blocking at long seq lengths and occasional context-invokes when cold keys miss the KV cache. We saw a few 200–300ms spikes when the cache had misses on prefix-heavy prompts.
[01:28] Lina: From security side — remind me what data gets into the cache? Is that customer PII ever kept? We need to validate retention and KMS usage.
[01:40] Connor: Lina, Redwood's pilot config for this account turned on ephemeral kv caching only, and we flagged that the cache TTL is short; but Jordan, you'll need to confirm in the Dedicated run that we can opt for no-persist or encrypt-at-rest via your KMS.
[01:55] Jordan: Yep, we can pass a test key. We'll want KMS/HSM integration for the production rollout.
[02:08] Alex: Ok good. Back to quality, Sam — can you walk us through the prompt cluster that regressed? You flagged the ‘long narrative digest’ set last week.
[02:15] Sam: Sure. So out of the 1,200 eval prompts, about 28 had consistent score drops (>8% KQI delta) on INT8. They are mostly multi-paragraph meeting notes that require factual condense and stitching. The model sometimes hallucinated details or dropped temporal ordering.
[02:36] Mei: For product, that delta is a blocker for our launch metric. We need <5% KQI deviation at pilot scale, otherwise we can't enable INT8 for the customer tier.
[02:48] Priya: Understood — a few immediate levers: 1) dynamic KV/prefix cache warm-up (hot-prefix caching) to reduce cold-miss artifacts, 2) targeted per-prompt fallback to FP8 for flagged prompts, 3) slight decoding temp/beam adjustments that reduce hallucinations but trade off creativity.
[03:10] Alex: Can you quantify the quality vs perf trade for option 2? Fallback on X% of requests — what does cost look like?
[03:21] Priya: Rough math — if 2% of traffic is fallback to FP8, cost delta is small (~+3–4% total), but latency for those requests goes up because FP8 on a different model variant has ~1.4x token latency. We can also do hybrid routes: run a cheap classifier that flags likely-hard prompts and route those to FP8.
[03:44] Sam: Classifier sounds good but needs training and we'd need to add an eval step to ensure it doesn't under-classify.
[03:50] Alex: Also need to keep unit economics in mind — Voltix has cadence of heavy night batch processing, that changes amortization of caching. Jordan, how bursty is their workload?
[03:58] Jordan: Very bursty. Morning ingestion window 2–4am UTC, then interactive users during US business hours. We'll see long sequences in both windows.
[04:10] Priya: That means hot-prefix caching will help in the interactive window, but batch will have higher cold miss rate unless you pre-warm cache for scheduled runs.
[04:25] [04:25] Speaker 5: (inaudible)
[04:32] Lina: For the Dedicated run, we'll need explicit language on data residency and audit logs. SOC 2 + ISO 27001 compliance are prerequisites for our procurement.
[04:45] Alex: Totally. We'll include the SOC 2 poster and the audit log attachment. Connor, can you confirm retention windows?
[04:52] Connor: We'll default to 7 days for logs in pilot, but can extend. I'll get a sample retention policy document out.
[05:03] Priya: Back to perf deltas — FP8 had slightly better KQIs on the long-form set, but the FP8 build we ran had model fusion kernels on our dev infra so it's faster than what you'd see on a stock instance. I want to run a controlled Dedicated A/B next week.
[05:25] Sam: Is FP8 generally safer quality-wise? I thought INT8 sometimes does better depending on quant scheme.
[05:32] Priya: It's model and workload dependent. For this model family we saw FP8 reduce token-level rounding error and a couple hallucination modes. INT8 gave better throughput but introduced some subtle context-binding errors for long dependencies.
[05:49] Alex: Let's go into the triage matrix you put in the sheet, Priya — you marked prompts as: hard-regress, borderline, noisy. Walk us through examples.
[06:00] Priya: Example A — meeting minutes that require chronological ordering; INT8 occasionally reordered events. Example B — dense factual extraction; we saw missing minute details. Example C — short Q&A, no regression. Hard-regress set is about 28 prompts, borderline ~60.
[06:25] Sam: On the hard-regress, can we isolate whether it's tokenization drift or cross-attention quant error?
[06:33] Priya: Early signals point to attention kernel quant error at long contexts. Tokenization seems consistent between runs. We'll attach profiler traces.
[06:45] Jordan: For the Dedicated run, how many GPUs do you recommend to replicate the p99 and throughput numbers?
[06:50] Priya: For realistic SLA stress, 4xA100 as a baseline for the pilot; that gives headroom to test autoscale and burst policies. For the 48h benchmark we can spin a 4xA100 pool and run mixed traffic.
[07:05] Mei: What about cost? Voltix needs a clear delta between Hosted INT8 and Dedicated cluster pricing.
[07:12] Alex: We'll provide a breakdown: per-token unit cost, amortized GPU cost for Dedicated, cache efficiency assumptions. I'll send a sample cost spreadsheet.
[07:22] [07:22] Speaker 1: (crosstalk)
[07:30] Sam: A practical Q — if we do the fallback classifier, how much latency does it add? We can't add >40ms to p50.
[07:37] Priya: If implemented as an in-line cheap model it adds ~10–30ms depending on sequence length. We can also run it asynchronously for batch jobs and pre-tag, which adds no interactive latency.
[07:50] Jordan: For VPC peering and KMS, what's the expected setup time on Redwood side?
[07:56] Alex: Typically 3–5 business days to configure Dedicated peering and test KMS integration, faster if you provide an infra contact and a service account.
[08:07] Lina: Procurement will want explicit SLA for p99 latency and uptime. Do you have sample SLA language?
[08:14] Connor: Yes, we have a pilot SLA template that covers uptime, incident response times, and remedies. We'll tailor it for Voltix needs.
[08:24] Priya: Quick note: one mitigation is a per-route soft-fallback policy. If INT8 output similarity drops below threshold for a prompt, route that prompt to FP8 next time. It's stateful but improves KQI while keeping most traffic on INT8.
[08:45] Mei: That sounds helpful if we can quantify false positives.
[08:51] Priya: We can include classifier ROC and expected FP/FN rates in the next deliverable.
[09:00] Alex: Ok let's capture the timeline: re-runs by 12/19, pilot Dedicated benchmark 12/22–12/23, SLA readout 12/23–12/24. Does that work?
[09:13] Jordan: Works for Infra. Procurement might take longer but ok for pilot.
[09:20] Sam: One more ask — for the re-run, can you include beam search off vs on? We saw decoding adjustments impacted hallucination.
[09:27] Priya: Yep, will include beam=1/2/4 and temperature sweeps.
[09:33] [09:33] Speaker 2: (brief audio glitch)
[09:41] Alex: Anything else on the technical side?
[09:44] Lina: Security will verify that ephemeral cache never persists to disk and that audit logs include prompt IDs, not raw prompt text. Also request for redaction tooling for PII in logs.
[09:58] Connor: We can add a redaction step and sample redaction policy.
[10:03] Priya: I'll add a config example for ephemeral-only cache + redaction flow.
[10:08] Alex: Great. Let's do a short recap. Priya will re-run INT8 w/ dynamic KV enabled and include profiler traces and beam/temp sweeps, deliverable 12/19. Sam will curate the 500-prompt sanitized regression set by 12/18. Jordan will provision Dedicated 4xA100 for 12/22 benchmark and provide KMS test key. Alex will send pilot pricing and sample SLA language by 12/18. Connor will share retention & audit sample docs.
[10:36] Sam: Thanks — on the curations, I'll tag the prompts with exemplar failure modes so SE can triage quicker.
[10:44] Priya: Also will run a small FP8 vs INT8 AB on the Dedicated pool so we can see real kernel parity.
[10:52] Alex: Perfect. We'll reconvene after the Dedicated pass — propose a follow-up on 2025-12-24 if that works for everyone, otherwise the week after.
[11:03] Jordan: 12/24 is tight because of holidays but a post-benchmark readout week of 12/29 could work.
[11:10] Alex: Noted. I'll send Doodle options. Thanks all.
[11:16] Connor: I'll ping the SOC 2 artifacts to Lina after the call.
[11:22] End of transcript.
